Maya (Docs): Hey team — opened a docs PR to add a migration snippet and clarify the rate limit/quotas wording. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4122

Samir (SDK): Thanks — link won't render in the sidebar if we use the long URL, can you add the short internal redirect? e.g., /docs/migration/usage-metrics -> redirects to the PR once merged.

Maya (Docs): Good call. Updated the PR to reference /docs/migration/usage-quota-migration. Also added an SDK snippet for retry/backoff around 429s. Could you sanity-check the snippet, Samir?

Samir (SDK): Quick look — two notes: (1) Our HTTP header names for remaining tokens are X-Usage-Remaining in hosted API, not X-RateLimit-Remaining. We should keep examples consistent with the API. (2) For the Node snippet, prefer streams for large responses.

Maya (Docs): Ok swapping to X-Usage-Remaining. I also added a small JS streaming example and a concise Python example for retries. Here's the JS snippet I added:
```js
// retry on 429 with exponential backoff
async function generateWithRetry(client, req, maxAttempts = 5) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < maxAttempts) {
    const res = await client.generate(req);
    if (res.status !== 429) return res;
    const waitMs = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attempt, 10000);
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, waitMs));
    attempt++;
  }
  throw new Error('rate limited after retries');
}
```

Samir (SDK): That looks fine. For the header read code, add a note showing how to parse the X-Usage-Remaining & X-Usage-Limit headers to power client-side backoff/buckets. Example: `const remaining = parseInt(res.headers['x-usage-remaining'] || '0', 10);`

Olivia (Billing): Quick question: PR mentions "token buckets by tier" — can we avoid internal jargon in public docs? Maybe rephrase to "usage allowance per plan" and include examples for Free/Pro/Enterprise. Also confirm metering units: are embeddings billed per vector or per 1k vectors?

Taylor (Product): Olivia is right — public docs should say "allowance". For metering units: embeddings are billed per vector in the billing system, but we expose a per-1k price on the pricing page. Docs should call out both: metering unit = vector, pricing listed per 1k vectors.

Maya (Docs): I'll update language to "allowance" and add a short callout: "Metering: system meters per vector; pricing often shown per 1,000 vectors." Anyone want a quick example table?

Olivia (Billing): Yes please — include example math for common cases: 150 vectors * price_per_1k = cost; show rounding behavior.

Maya (Docs): Added a tiny worked example: "150 vectors => 0.15 * price_per_1k". Also linked to billing FAQ.

Docs Bot: CI started for PR #4122 (build/docs) — status will update in thread.

CI Bot: build/docs #4122 passed — 9 checks succeeded.

Samir (SDK): One more nit: The migration guide suggests renaming rate_limit to quota in config. That will break older SDK clients. Maybe recommend a deprecation path: accept both keys and log a warning for one release before removing.

Maya (Docs): Good catch — added a migration note with exact example config and a recommended deprecation timeline. Example snippet I added for backward-compatible config: 
```yaml
# config v2 (supports both keys)
quota:
  requests_per_minute: 120
# legacy
rate_limit: 120  # deprecated, kept for v1 clients
```

Samir (SDK): Perfect. I'll add a small SDK patch to accept rate_limit and map it to quota, and emit a warning in v3.1.0.

Taylor (Product): Also let's be explicit about dashboard links — the old /dash/usage link is being replaced by /console/usage-v2. Maya please add a redirect note and update the broken internal link we found.

Maya (Docs): Done — updated the doc and fixed the broken link inside the Usage -> Dashboards section.

Olivia (Billing): After merge, I'll run a quick audit to ensure pricing pages and docs use consistent metering language.

Maya (Docs): Thanks all. I think this is review-ready after the small SDK change. Requesting final review from Samir and Olivia.

Samir (SDK): Reviewing now, should be able to approve after my tiny client patch lands.

Olivia (Billing): Approved from billing side (language and math look correct).

Maya (Docs): Merged — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/9b1c6a2. Leaving a post-merge checklist in the PR for the redirect and SDK release notes.

Docs Bot: PR #4122 merged by Maya (Docs).
